conventions.convention: The model uses conforming scalar P1 elements on matching two-dimensional polygonal subdomains, positive coefficients constant on each subdomain, and homogeneous values on a nonempty outer Dirichlet segment. H/h is max_i H_i/h_i.
A floating block is the local energy before any outer-boundary values are fixed. The empty interior block is an invertible operator on the zero vector space.
The jump map has kernel equal to the conforming trace space. Redundant multipliers are represented by Λ = range B with its inherited Euclidean inner product.
For the two-dimensional estimate all polygon vertices are primal, and each remaining open-edge node has exactly two incident subdomains.
E0 maps partial traces to conforming traces; R is inclusion, E0 R = I, and the coefficient weight of copy i is ρ_i/(ρ_i+ρ_j).
The scaled right inverse B_D^T selects the unique representative in ker(R E0), giving B B_D^T = I and B_D^T B = I − R E0.
The boundary fractional seminorm uses Euclidean distance |s−t| in its denominator and is taken modulo constants.
Only eigenvalues other than 1 must match with multiplicity. The condition-number theorem assumes nonzero assembled and multiplier spaces and asserts no condition number for a zero-dimensional solve.

load_bearing.statement: For a continuous piecewise-linear boundary trace g on a model polygon with matching quasiuniform P1 mesh, cρ_i|g|²_(1/2,∂Ω_i) ≤ g^T S_i g ≤ Cρ_i|g|²_(1/2,∂Ω_i), with constants depending only on the fixed polygon shape, mesh shape-regularity and quasiuniformity.

Under the scalar model, all subdomain vertices primal, and coefficient-scaled averaging, P = I − R E0 satisfies ||Pw||²_S̃ ≤ C(1+log(H/h))²||w||²_S̃ for every w ∈ W̃, independently of coefficient jumps, mesh size, subdomain diameter and subdomain count.

The edge cutoff has squared 00,E norm at most C(1+log(H/h)); every continuous piecewise-affine u_h satisfies the stated mean-zero discrete L∞ estimate; consequently its interpolated cutoff product after subtracting the edge mean has squared 00,E norm at most C(1+log(H_i/h_i))²||∇u_h||².

The floating local kernel on a connected subdomain consists exactly of constants; the zero-boundary interior stiffness block is positive definite, including the empty-block convention; the assembled global Dirichlet stiffness matrix is positive definite.

A primal vertex fixed in each floating local component's dual subproblem makes its local dual stiffness positive definite. With all subdomain vertices primal and nonempty global Dirichlet boundary, the partially assembled interface energy is positive definite.
For finite-dimensional real spaces, SPD A, and L,T satisfying LT = I_U, every eigenvalue of (LA⁻¹L^T)(T^TAT) lies in [1, ||TL||²_A], with the stated vacuous zero-space convention.
For SPD A and maps satisfying L_i T_i = I and T_1 L_1 + T_2 L_2 = I, the displayed primal and dual products have identical eigenvalues with multiplicity except possibly at 1.
For every admissible local trace g_i, H_i g_i is the unique finite-element lift minimizing local energy, and its minimum energy is g_i^T S_i g_i.

concerns.concern: The uniform geometric hypothesis needs adjudication. Step 1.1 asserts: 'The finite chart count and chart constants are uniform under [F1].' The model explicitly supplies bounded side count, lower corner-angle bounds, inradius comparable to diameter and 'a uniform interior-cone parameter', but does not define a uniform boundary graph/neighborhood radius. A pointwise interior-cone condition alone does not justify this assertion. Consider Ω_ε = ((−1,1)×(0,2)) minus the closed notch [−ε/2,ε/2]×[1,2]. These eight-sided polygons have uniformly bounded diameter, comparable inradius, right/reentrant-right angles and pointwise interior cones of fixed aperture and height. On aligned quasiuniform meshes define the P1 function to be zero below y=1, −φ(y) on the left arm and +φ(y) on the right arm, where φ rises linearly from 0 to 1 on [1,5/4] and is 1 above 5/4. Its energy for ρ=1 is 4(2−ε) ≤ 8, and it satisfies zero Dirichlet data on the bottom side. Its trace differs by 2 on the facing notch segments of length L=3/4. Just one ordered cross-boundary contribution to the stated Euclidean-distance seminorm is 8[(L/ε) arctan(L/ε) − (1/2)log(1+(L/ε)²)], which diverges as ε⁻¹. Harmonic minimality therefore contradicts a uniform positive lower trace-Schur constant under those explicit bounds. Unless 'uniform interior-cone parameter' is intended to impose a stronger uniform local boundary-chart condition excluding this family, the uniform claim is false. The same geometry also challenges the uniform cross-edge-integral assertion in lem-pe26-scaled-averaging-energy-bound, step 1.1; its downstream condition-number proof needs disposition. The consulted source retains domain-dependent trace constants: [Rheinbach, Theorem 1.1.1, printed p. 13](https://d-nb.info/983219192/34).
